# needle.server

> needle.server turns plain language into tool calls. You send text plus the tools your app exposes; it answers with a well-formed JSON tool call and a confidence score. It runs Cactus Needle 3, a tiny (29-121M parameter) on-device model that does tool calling and nothing else: it never writes prose. One HTTP endpoint, no authentication, no sessions, no SDK.

This file is written for AI coding assistants. It is enough to write a correct client without reading the source. Copy the patterns; do not invent fields that are not listed here. The exact schema is at `GET /openapi.json` on a running server. Upstream's guides cover the model itself: tool design at https://cactuscompute.com/blog/designing-tools-for-needle and confidence at https://cactuscompute.com/blog/needle-confidence.

Default base URL: `http://<host>:4007`.

## The one endpoint

`POST /complete` with a JSON body:

```json
{
  "input": "dim the living room to 30",
  "tools": [{
    "name": "set_lights",
    "description": "Turn a room's lights on or off and set brightness",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "room": {"type": "string"},
        "on": {"type": "boolean"},
        "brightness": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 100}
      },
      "required": ["room", "on"]
    }
  }],
  "system": "locale: en-US; device: speaker",
  "history": []
}
```

- `input` (string, required) - the latest thing to act on: the user's words, or, after you ran a tool, the results as a JSON string (see Multi-turn).
- `tools` (array, required, 1 to 20) - JSON-schema tool definitions. The compact form above and the OpenAI form (`{"type": "function", "function": {...}}`) both work.
- `system` (string, optional) - facts about the environment, never instructions. See System facts.
- `history` (array of strings, optional) - your earlier `input` values in this conversation, oldest first. See Multi-turn.

Unknown fields are ignored.

## The response

The engine's own envelope, unchanged, plus a `server` object:

```json
{
  "type": "call",
  "success": true,
  "error": null,
  "error_code": null,
  "reason": null,
  "function_calls": [{"name": "set_lights", "arguments": {"room": "living room", "on": true, "brightness": 30}}],
  "suppressed_calls": [],
  "reasoning": "'living room' -> room; '30' -> brightness",
  "confidence": 0.94,
  "validation": {"ungrounded": [], "negation": false},
  "prefill_tps": 2300.0,
  "decode_tps": 1200.0,
  "peak_ram_mb": 92.5,
  "server": {"worker": "warm", "replayed_turns": 0, "dropped_history": 0, "queue_ms": 0.1, "engine_ms": 41.0}
}
```

- `function_calls` - a list of `{"name", "arguments"}`, in the order to run them. `arguments` is an object (not a string) and is grammar-guaranteed to match your schema.
- `type` - `"call"` when the model wants tools run (an empty `function_calls` is a refusal); `"respond"` when the exchange is finished, which is what you get after feeding back tool results. There is never any text to show the user.
- `confidence` - calibrated score in [0, 1]. You must gate on it; see below.
- `suppressed_calls` - a call the engine withheld because its confidence was under 0.1. `function_calls` is then empty. Offer it to the user to confirm, or treat the turn as a refusal.
- `reasoning` - a terse derivation of each argument. Useful in logs and confirmation prompts, not as an answer.
- `validation.ungrounded` - `tool.field` names whose value does not appear literally in the input. Advisory: a date the model resolved from "tomorrow" is listed here even though it is correct.
- `server.worker` - `warm` (an engine already held this toolset), `spawned` or `replaced` (one had to start; slower).
- `server.dropped_history` - how many of your `history` entries were not replayed because of the limits.

## Behaviour contract (read this before writing code)

- The server is stateless. Nothing is remembered between requests. A conversation exists only in the `history` you send.
- An off-topic or unsupported request returns an empty `function_calls`. That is the refusal. There is no free-text fallback; always handle the empty case.
- Arguments contain only values evidenced in the input. Optional fields with no evidence are omitted, not guessed. Never assume an optional key exists.
- One request can produce several calls ("turn off the lights and lock the door"); run them in order.
- A high confidence is not a guarantee. Wrong calls have been observed at 0.86. Anything destructive or irreversible deserves a confirmation regardless of the score.
- Keep conversations short. The model reliably uses the last few turns only; recall of older turns fails without any error.

## Confidence gating

Pick a threshold per product. Upstream suggests acting at 0.7 and above:

```python
calls, held = r["function_calls"], r["suppressed_calls"]
if calls and r["confidence"] >= 0.7:
    execute(calls)                           # sure: act
elif calls or held:
    confirm(calls or held, r["reasoning"])   # unsure: show the call, ask
else:
    say("I can't do that here")              # nothing to do: refuse
```

## Multi-turn

Only needed when a later call depends on an earlier result ("create a note", then "delete that note"). Feed each tool result back as the next `input`, as a JSON string holding a list with one result per call, and list every earlier `input` in `history`:

```python
history = []

r = complete(input="create a note titled groceries", history=history)
results = [run(call) for call in r["function_calls"]]      # e.g. [{"note_id": 48213}]
history.append("create a note titled groceries")

r = complete(input=json.dumps(results), history=history)   # r["type"] == "respond"
history.append(json.dumps(results))

r = complete(input="actually delete that note", history=history)
# -> delete_note(note_id=48213)
```

- `history` holds your inputs only: user text and tool-result JSON strings. Never put the model's answers in it. The server replays your inputs into a fresh engine session and the model regenerates its own side, deterministically.
- Send the same `tools` and `system` for every request of one conversation.
- Each replayed turn costs about as much as a normal request, so a long history is a slow request.
- If `input` is a tool result, `history` must contain the request that led to it.

## System facts

`system` is a `key: value; key: value` string of facts. Recognised keys: `date`, `locale`, `device`, `battery`, `network`, `location`, `user`, `assistant`. Instructions ("You are a helpful assistant") do nothing useful.

- The server adds today's date (`date: 2026-09-17 Thu`) unless your `system` already contains `date:`. Relative dates ("tomorrow") resolve against it. Send your own `date: 2026-09-17 Thu 14:30` if you need the time of day or another time zone.
- `tools` and `system` together identify an engine. Keep both byte-identical between requests to stay on a warm engine. Do not put anything that changes per request (a timestamp, a request id) in `system`.

## Designing tools

- Five tools or fewer per request works best. Above five the engine picks the five most relevant per turn, and starting an engine for a big toolset is slow (about 1 s for 20 tools against 0.1 s for 3).
- One tool per action, named the way a user would say it. Put formats in descriptions. Put constraints in the schema (`enum`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `pattern`), because the decode grammar enforces them.
- A request for one product area should send only that area's tools. Different toolsets are cheap: that is what this server is for.

## Limits and errors

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| `input` length | 2,000 characters |
| `input` plus replayed history | 4,000 characters |
| replayed history turns | 6 (oldest dropped first) |
| `tools` | 1 to 20, at most 32,000 characters of JSON |
| `system` length | 500 characters |
| time to answer | 5 s |

Errors are `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`:

| Status | `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `input_empty`, `input_too_long` | Fix the input. An over-long input is never cut, because half a command gives a confident wrong call. |
| 400 | `tools_required`, `too_many_tools`, `tools_too_large`, `tools_invalid`, `tools_rejected` | Fix the tools. Every tool needs a string `name`, and `parameters` must be a JSON-schema object. `tools_rejected` means the engine could not load the schemas. |
| 400 | `system_too_long`, `tool_result_without_history` | Fix the request. |
| 422 | (FastAPI validation body) | A field is missing or has the wrong type. |
| 429 | `queue_full` | The server is busy. Retry after the `Retry-After` header (seconds). |
| 503 | `worker_failed`, `unavailable` | An engine failed or no memory is left. Retry. |
| 504 | `deadline_exceeded` | The engine took too long. Send less text or fewer tools. |

History that does not fit is dropped silently, oldest first, and counted in `server.dropped_history`.

## Speed

On an Apple M4 Pro: about 40 ms per request on a warm engine. The first request for a new toolset adds about 0.1 s (3 tools) to 1 s (20 tools). Two requests run at a time; the rest queue briefly. Idle engines stop after 10 minutes.

## Other endpoints

- `GET /health` - `{"status": "ok", "model": "needle3", "workers": ..., "busy": ..., "memory_mb": ..., "queued": ...}`; status 503 when the engine files are missing.
- `GET /models` - `{"object": "list", "data": [{"id": "needle3", ...}]}`.
- `GET /llms.txt` - this file. `GET /openapi.json` - the exact schema.

## Minimal clients

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:4007/complete -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "input": "lock the front door",
  "tools": [{"name": "lock_door", "description": "Lock a door",
             "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"door": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["door"]}}]
}'
```

```python
import httpx

def complete(input, tools, system=None, history=()):
    r = httpx.post("http://localhost:4007/complete", timeout=15,
                   json={"input": input, "tools": tools, "system": system, "history": list(history)})
    if r.status_code == 429:
        raise RuntimeError(f"busy, retry in {r.headers['Retry-After']} s")
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()
```

```ts
async function complete(input: string, tools: object[], system?: string, history: string[] = []) {
  const r = await fetch("http://localhost:4007/complete", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ input, tools, system, history }),
  });
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${r.status} ${(await r.json()).error?.code}`);
  return r.json(); // { function_calls, confidence, suppressed_calls, reasoning, ... }
}
```

## Common mistakes

- Expecting a text answer. There is none, ever. An empty `function_calls` is the model saying no.
- Executing `function_calls` without looking at `confidence`.
- Putting the model's previous answers, or OpenAI-style message objects, in `history`. It takes your earlier inputs as plain strings.
- Parsing `arguments` as a string. It is already an object.
- Changing `system` on every request, which forces a new engine each time.
- Sending every tool your app has. Send the few that fit the moment.
